data.title: Nvidia Faces Risk of Losing Key Engineers After Jensen Huang's Ouster
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Business Insider, Nvidia faces a risk of losing key engineers after its board removed Jensen Huang last week. Melius Research technology analyst Ben Reitzes said ahead of Nvidia's earnings call that retaining engineers and maintaining the product roadmap are issues for the interim management team. Nvidia's market capitalization has fallen by about $500 billion since Huang's removal, the report said.

Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress told employees at an all-hands meeting on Wednesday that the company would bring forward salary increases and additional stock awards to December. Nvidia also said its technology plans and customer relationships remain stable. The board is considering internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO role. Thousands of employees have signed an open letter calling for Huang's reinstatement, while Nvidia robotics researcher Darrell Dai resigned after Huang's departure, the report said.

data.title: Sky Founder-Linked Wallet Borrows 77 Million USDS as Pool Liquidity Runs Out
data.description: A wallet linked to Sky founder Rune Christensen deposited about $185 million worth of SKY tokens as collateral on the Sky protocol and borrowed about 77 million USDS. According to Foresight News, on-chain analyst kirbycrypto said the borrowing represents nearly 50% of the protocol’s total value locked, while utilization has reached 100% and available liquidity for lender withdrawals has fallen to zero. Lenders must wait for repayments or new funds to enter the pool. The associated wallet has not actively repaid the debt for about six months, and its outstanding balance has continued to grow.

data.title: Rogo Completes $350 Million Financing at $3.75 Billion Valuation

data.title: Fed Minutes Flag AI Debt as a Fresh Inflation and Stability Risk
data.description: Federal Reserve officials put artificial intelligence at the center of their policy concerns in October, casting AI-driven demand as "a material source of inflation risk" and warning that the debt financing the buildout has grown fast, opaque and concentrated. The minutes, released Wednesday, show that most participants said AI-related debt had grown rapidly, much of it through complex and opaque structures, and a few noted that exposure is concentrating among a small number of companies.On policy, almost all participants judged that further increases in the target range "would likely be appropriate" to bring inflation back to 2% on time. The FOMC voted 10-2 to hold at 3.75% to 4%, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point move. A couple of participants raised the possibility of a larger increase in December.Officials also said they expect inflation to fall sharply in 2027 and beyond as current shocks fade.

data.title: Trump Administration Launches Center to Stop Scam Payments
data.description:
The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has launched a Threat Disruption Center to disrupt money flows to foreign criminal networks involved in scams, cybercrime and sextortion. According to Cointelegraph, the Homeland Security Task Force’s National Coordination Center announced the unit’s launch on Wednesday. Co-led by the departments of Homeland Security and Justice, the center is intended to coordinate more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners. They will track scams and work with banks and cryptocurrency platforms to stop payments to scam networks. The Homeland Security statement said the center was established under a March 2026 executive order directing federal agencies to work with private companies to combat online fraud and other cybercrime targeting Americans. FBI Criminal Branch operations director Heith Janke said that delays between a victim’s report and a response give criminals more time to launder stolen funds and find additional targets. The initiative is focused on acting faster to disrupt those financial flows and coordinate responses across public agencies and private-sector partners.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs was selected as the center’s primary private-sector partner. It will provide and maintain Ardence, an investigative platform intended to map scam networks and identify victims, and will supply engineering and investigative support. TRM co-founder and CEO Esteban Castano said scammers may continue taking payments from victims over months or years, draining savings or retirement funds. He said earlier intervention could include warning victims before another payment, removing scam websites before they target other families, or freezing stolen funds while recovery remains possible. The FBI received about 453,000 reports of online fraud in 2025, with reported losses exceeding $17.7 billion. In September, the Justice Department estimated that overseas scam centers cost Americans about $10 billion a year. The department’s estimate included losses from schemes such as cryptocurrency and online investment fraud. The center’s work will involve coordination with financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms as authorities seek to identify scam activity and interrupt payments to criminal networks.

data.title: Reciprocal Ventures Invests in Live-Streaming Prediction Market CRSH
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Reciprocal Ventures announced an investment in CRSH, a prediction-market platform built around livestreams where users can forecast outcomes in games, challenges and other events. An investor at Reciprocal Ventures said the firm met CRSH founders Evan Rama and Param Patel during the Monad Accelerator and described the team as experienced in product development and streamer outreach.

CRSH curates markets and has rules barring streamers from betting on their own actions, allowing disputed outcomes to be reviewed and voiding markets if manipulation is detected. The platform currently aggregates streamer content from other services and plans to develop streamer partnerships and original shows. Markets can cover specific livestream outcomes, such as the number of player eliminations.

data.title: CertiK Completes Independent Verification of GL1 Self-Assessment Statements
data.description:
CertiK has completed an independent technical verification of self-assessment statements submitted by the XRP Ledger Foundation and Partior for Global Layer One (GL1). According to Odaily, the review covered the “Architecture” and “Resilience” principles in GL1’s Market Infrastructure Toolkit (MI Toolkit), providing financial institutions with additional technical information for assessing the underlying networks.

For financial institutions considering the networks, the review adds evidence to help them understand how the infrastructure operates and assess whether its controls meet their requirements. For network operators, independent technical verification can increase the transparency of self-assessment statements and support them with technical evidence.

data.title: LUKSO Email Recovery Vulnerability Leads to Theft of 1.4 Million LYX From About 300 Accounts
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, attackers exploited a backend vulnerability in LUKSO’s email recovery system overnight from Nov. 17 to 18, gaining control of about 300 Universal Profile accounts and stealing approximately 1.4 million LYX. They moved the tokens to Ethereum through a cross-chain bridge and exchanged them for about 50 ETH on decentralized exchanges, including Uniswap.

LUKSO said the flaw allowed attackers to take control of the recovery service’s own “recovery” Universal Profile and add their control keys to user accounts before transferring assets. The LUKSO blockchain and Universal Profile smart contracts were not affected, and no private keys or seed phrases were exposed. Accounts that did not use email recovery were unaffected. LUKSO has disabled the email recovery system; file-based and device keychain backups remain safe.

Affected users must remove the attackers’ control keys and the malicious “recovery-UP” controller in sequence; revoking permissions alone is insufficient. LUKSO said users can retain their accounts, names, history, and remaining assets after completing the steps. The project is preparing a compensation plan and expects to announce details in the coming weeks.

data.title: Variational Co-Founder Says New Funding Will Expand Swaps and Bring Institutional Derivatives Onchain
data.description:
Variational co-founder Edward Yu said $110 million in new funding will be used mainly to expand the company’s swap business and bring institutional-grade derivatives onchain. According to Odaily, the expansion will raise open interest limits, improve liquidity, add tradable assets and broaden the range of asset classes.

The company’s Pro version will develop a flexible multi-dealer network supporting derivatives that can be settled peer to peer. Variational plans to offer swaps, perpetual contracts, options and other derivatives across thousands of markets. Yu said financial markets will undergo major changes in the coming years.

data.title: Citigroup Cuts Bitcoin and Ethereum Base-Case Targets to $99,532 and $2,838
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Block, Citigroup lowered its base-case price targets for Bitcoin to $99,532 and Ethereum to $2,838 after a further decline in crypto markets. Citi strategist Alex Saunders attributed the cuts to weaker ETF demand, deleveraging in futures markets, a stronger U.S. dollar, rising real yields, and increased stock-market volatility.
